title: Chapter 1: It Seems the Duchess is Coming to Marry 1
content: I, Lagna Vel Brave, was being swamped with the miscellaneous tasks of a rural noble in the frontier.
“Damn it, damn it, damn it! How did it come to this?!”
In my study, I cursed under my breath as I sifted through a mountain of handover documents, hastily scribbling my signature in the appropriate places.
“Where’s the red ink?! This is a world with magic, so it should exist!”
In this world, despite the presence of magic, there are no seals.
There’s sealing wax, but it’s only used for special correspondence.
“Why doesn’t anyone notice? I’m going to get tendonitis!”
The sensation in my right hand, which had been moving endlessly, was already gone, and I was somehow managing to work through it with recovery magic.
“Ugh, I’m done for. My right hand is dead. It’s numb.”
I recalled the time I was bitten by a magic bug with paralysis poison, but this mountain of documents was far more vicious than that.
“Damn you, old man! Why did you have to die...”
This situation, being overwhelmed by unfamiliar paperwork, was a result of the war that had occurred about a month ago.

Our enemy country, which shares a border with us, invaded, and to make matters worse, there was also a riot of monsters, throwing the frontier territory into chaos, and my father was killed in battle.
To add insult to injury, both my elder brothers also died in that conflict.
Now, as the only surviving third son, I was suddenly thrust into inheriting this frontier territory, lamenting over the mountain of paperwork that had piled up.
“I was planning to become an adventurer and live a carefree life!”
In this world, aside from magic, there are adventurers and dungeons, and as the third son of a rural noble, I was destined to be cast aside without even attending the academy in the royal capital.
I had intended to live my second life in a chaotic manner, taking advantage of my position, but how did it come to this?
While managing a territory and dealing with paperwork that didn’t suit me, I also had to attend the academy in the royal capital.
“It’s impossible, way too impossible.”
This was the frontier territory, and considering the distance to the royal capital, I had to live in a dormitory, which made me feel faint.
Currently, I was delaying my enrollment due to family funerals and the aftermath of the war, but could I really just pretend I forgot and refuse to enroll?
“Probably not, right? Definitely not…”
If I broke such customs, I would lose support from the higher-ranking nobles living in the royal capital.
The Brave Territory, while rich in natural resources, was infested with monsters, and skirmishes with the neighboring enemy country occurred frequently.
Due to the land’s characteristics, there was an abundance of monster materials, and businesses catering to adventurers and drifters thrived, but self-sufficiency was non-existent.

“Even if I cultivate fields, they’ll just get burned by the enemy country, and even if I develop the mountains, goblins and orcs will come in droves to wreak havoc like they’re avenging their parents!”
Because of such circumstances, I was entirely reliant on noble support, and most of the documents piling up were related to aid supplies.
It felt like a trade-off for stopping monsters and enemy soldiers.
“Well, I guess I have no choice but to do it…”
I steeled myself for the daily grind of buttering up the other noble sons at the academy, begging for their support.
“Can I even do this?”
Imagining the days of bowing my head, which I didn’t want to do, made me feel nauseous.
“After all, I’ve been educated solely to kill monsters and enemy soldiers from one to ten, right? This is a blood-soaked territory!”
I knew what other nobles called the Brave Territory.
Discarded Land, discarded land. It couldn’t even develop infrastructure.
Saying it myself made me feel sad, but I understood that was just how it was.
In the Brave Territory, human lives were cheap.
I couldn’t even mourn for my father and brothers, who were killed by the enemy country.
“Today, you’re particularly grumbling, aren’t you?”
As I was venting my frustrations while furiously working on the documents, the butler of the Brave Family, Sebas, peeked in through the door.
“Master Lagna, I have an important matter to discuss.”
“You came at a good time, Sebas. Help me out. And stop calling me ‘Master,’ just call me Lagna.”
“You haven’t officially inherited yet. Moreover, these are documents that must be reviewed by the lord, so it’s not something a mere vassal like me can assist with.”
“Tch.”
I couldn’t help but click my tongue, but Sebas was busy as well.
He handled all the correspondence with other nobles related to us, allowing me to avoid the most time-consuming and labor-intensive task of meeting with the nobles providing support.
But the way he said it was irritating!
“So, what’s this important matter?”
“Hmm, I must say I’m surprised that there is, after all, a bloodline capable of handling paperwork in the Brave Family?”
“…Is that really why you came to tell me?”
See? It’s irritating, right?
My father and brothers were indeed the type who couldn’t handle paperwork at all.
That’s why they had specialized servants to help with it, but all those valuable individuals had perished in battle.
Damn it!
I had expected this, so there was no point in being upset.
While I felt a bit sad, in this land where skirmishes with people and monsters were constant, we had been raised to accept things as they were.
It was just a matter of whether it was early or late.
“Actually, there’s a marriage proposal for you.”
“A marriage proposal? Isn’t that a bit sudden?”
I was taken aback by the unexpected words.
I understood that becoming a lord would bring such discussions, but marriage proposals to the Brave Territory, known as the discarded land, were generally avoided by everyone.
“The fiancées of the first and second sons didn’t even show up for the funerals!”
It was a harsh reality, but it was a land that was dangerous and despised.
“When I went to report, they seemed quite relieved.”
“…I could kill you.”
I snapped my pen in half.
I felt as if the pride of the soldiers who died protecting the country had been tarnished.
“That’s not good, Master.”
Sebas, as if he had anticipated this, immediately offered me a replacement pen, shrugging his shoulders as he continued.
“If there are no connections, we won’t be able to survive. You shouldn’t say you’ll kill someone just because you’re upset.”
“Isn’t she just some woman no one would want? That’s why she’s being married off to us.”
If I killed such people, no one would complain.
They’d pretend to be angry, but deep down, they’d be relieved that the troublesome property had been disposed of.
“So, what kind of troublemaker is this fiancée?”
“Goodness, if you approach women with unnecessary preconceptions, you’ll get burned, Master.”
I glared at Sebas, thinking he was the one who provoked me, but he just brushed it off.
For now, I should refuse the marriage proposal.
In a situation where I didn’t even know my mother’s face, I couldn’t imagine a wife.
“Sebas, as you can see, we’re piled up with all sorts of things and super busy. You understand, right? Can’t you just casually refuse on that basis?”
Since I had to inherit this territory, I knew I would eventually have to think seriously about a wife, but it was just too early.

“After all, I have to head to the royal capital academy, which is quite far from the Brave Territory, once the aftermath is over. I’ll have to butter up a bunch of nobles at a school attended by many, and during long breaks, I’ll be back to deal with the unfamiliar work of a lord?”
Even though I had managed to prepare for dealing with troublesome monsters and enemy countries ahead of time, I was still overwhelmed with matters concerning the territory and the academy.
“It’s impossible. I’ll refuse. Yes, I’ll refuse with a heavy heart.”
“That’s impossible.”
An immediate rejection; couldn’t he have at least softened his wording a bit?
“I don’t think it’ll lead to a good marriage…”
“Haha, whether I marry or not, it won’t change anything. No lady will settle in the Brave Territory.”
“That’s not something to laugh about…”
I felt a chill at the horrific situation, but I kept trying to come up with excuses.

“Sebas, I don’t have any time to rest. In a year, the monsters will increase again, and there’s a possibility that the enemy country, healed from their wounds, will invade again without learning their lesson, you know?”

“I apologize for interrupting your desperate reasoning, Master, but this marriage proposal comes from the Oldwood Duke’s family, who will provide more support in weapons and food than any other noble family, so it’s impossible to refuse.”
“Huh?!”
I instinctively crushed the pen I was holding at Sebas’s words.
“Oh no, a new pen!”
“Goodness gracious.”
“I don’t understand. Sebas, tell me our title.”
“You’re a count, ranked fifth in the court hierarchy. You can technically marry into a duke’s family.”
“Add ‘from the frontier’ to that, ‘from the frontier!’”
Hearing the title alone was one thing, but the prefix ‘from the frontier’ was attached.
Just that alone, just that alone, gave the Brave Territory its nickname of discarded land.
The title was given solely to make us take on the responsibility of dealing with monsters and skirmishes with enemy countries, and I had never been treated as a high-ranking noble.
“Why would a duke’s family be involved with us… oh.”
At that moment, I recalled what kind of world this was.
I knew this world.
It was the same world as the game I happened to play in my previous life.
“Master, what’s wrong?”
“N-nothing.”
In a distant past, I lived in a country called Japan and died somewhere.
I couldn’t remember the reason for my death or my original name, but I remembered the facts.
When I was three years old, I remembered being knocked out by an orc.
At first, I was confused by the strange memories, but when I heard the name of the country, I realized.
—Ah, this is an isekai reincarnation.
I had been so busy with daily life that I had completely forgotten.
At first, I was excited about the idea of being reincarnated in another world, but the reality was vastly different from what I had imagined.
This was a family that taught how to hunt monsters and kill people from the age of three; it was only natural.
Day after day, I was thrust into battles with monsters, occasionally dragged into skirmishes with enemy countries—essentially, wars.
I had been desperately living to survive, and before I knew it, I was fifteen, somehow the heir to the lordship.
“Indeed… it was that kind of time… the generations match too…”
“Master, do you know something?”
“Nothing at all!”

As I held my head in my hands, searching my memories in front of Sebas, I recalled that this world was about a commoner girl protagonist who was recognized for her talent and attended a noble academy, where she developed a romantic relationship with handsome characters who were targets for romance—essentially, it was a dating sim.
The name Oldwood appeared in that dating sim as well—as the villainous noble girl who bullied the protagonist.
That event must have happened not long ago.

The duke’s fiancée, who was originally engaged to the prince, bullied the protagonist, who was flirting with the prince, leading to a duel, and the defeated duke’s fiancée had her engagement annulled on the spot.
It was a typical event.
After losing the duel, the duke’s fiancée was made to take responsibility and married off to a rural noble, facing a tragic fate.
That’s how it was depicted in the story, but…
“That was my family?!”
My shout echoed through the not-so-large mansion of an upper noble.
Ever since I learned that the duke’s fiancée, who had her engagement annulled, was coming to marry me, I had been racking my brain to remember what kind of game that was.
Though it was a game aimed at girls, it was packed with battles, dungeons, and various other elements, almost as if they had crammed everything they could into it.
In the final stages, the royal capital, where the story took place, was engulfed in flames.
The Brave Territory faced invasions from the enemy country we had been desperately dealing with, and a massive army of monsters surged forth.
“D-despair is all I see…”
I buried my face in my pillow, grumbling, but my recent mornings had been like this.
If the beings we had been desperately fighting against were now pouring into the royal capital, what would happen to the Brave Territory?
That’s right, it would perish.
I had been so focused on surviving daily life that I had forgotten, but the only salvation for a family destined to perish was being born as the third son.
I had no responsibilities as a noble and would eventually be cast aside.
That’s why the young Lagna had dreams.
To become an adventurer and traverse the world with nothing but his trained body.
Not as the protagonist of a story or even as a mob character in the academy.
Because I was far removed from the progression of the story, both geographically and in terms of plot, I genuinely believed I could enjoy the concept of another world.
“Master Lagna, you must prepare yourself. They will be arriving soon.”
“...I’m sleeping.”
As I sulked in bed, realizing the harshness of reality, Sebas entered my room with a few subordinate servants in tow.
“Those who are sleeping don’t say they’re sleeping. That’s a strange thing to say.”
“Waaah! Am I even here? Just do your thing over there!”
“Even though she’s someone whose engagement was annulled, she’s still a higher-ranking duchess, you know? You must maintain her dignity.”
“Ugh.”
I was forcibly dragged out of bed and made to change into a stiff formal outfit.
I really disliked this outfit because it was hard to move in...
I should have been out of the house by now, enjoying being an adventurer and exploring dungeons, so how did it come to this?
Just doing the lord’s work and going to the academy was tough enough, and now I had to deal with a duchess coming to marry me without any prior notice.
This was truly a case of adding insult to injury.
“Master, please be sure not to make any blunders.”
“I know.”
The name of the duchess was Alicia Gran Oldwood.
With translucent silver hair, she was tall, busty, beautiful, and intelligent.
Despite being treated as a villainous noble girl, she wasn’t academically poor or a dropout; she was a smart woman.
Having undergone elite education since childhood to become the prince’s partner, she was somewhat similar to me in a different way.
But her personality was terrible.
The reason for her defeat was likely her impulsive nature.

She had a strong sense of elitism and often berated the protagonist with things like, “Commoners should know their place,” and “Even if status doesn’t matter at the academy, once you step outside, remember you are a noble or a commoner,” in a loud voice.

There were various lines she used to bully others, and I often thought while playing the game how she could do such things with her entourage, but now I thought it was somewhat understandable given her noble status.
Nobles have a sense of pride, and the status of their family is absolute.
I had a different common sense from this world, and given the nature of the Brave Territory, I thought that whether commoners or nobles, it didn’t matter; once dead, they were just meat.
But nobles in this world valued customs and traditions, and when it came to royalty, there was no way a commoner could marry them.
Even in the Japan I lived in during my previous life, it was required that anyone marrying the Emperor be someone the citizens could accept.

Of course, at the end of the story, there’s a twist where the protagonist turns out to be of a noble bloodline that was lost, and everyone flips their opinions, but at the beginning, no one knows that.
The tumultuous history of the royal capital is often sparked by such typical developments, and in a sense, the duchess could be considered a victim.
“Sebas.”
“What is it, Master?”
While organizing the information about the duchess, I asked Sebas.
“What will a noble girl born into a higher-ranking family and raised solely for the crown prince become in this busy Brave Territory?”

“Perhaps a means of getting rid of her and a warning? It wouldn’t be surprising if people thought that Alicia-sama’s failure to keep the prince was the reason. After all, she caused a duel and lost spectacularly.”
It meant that things had reached a point where there was no turning back.
“Hey, are we being used as a means of getting rid of her and a warning?”
“The mortality rate is high, after all. The Brave Territory has a reputation for it.”
Even though I was being mocked, Sebas had a look on his face as if it were the most natural thing in the world.
I began to doubt if he was truly the butler of the Brave Family.
“Master Lagna, think carefully.”
“What?”
“The duke is well aware of the situation in the Brave Family. Although it has come to this, this will strengthen the ties with the duke’s family to some extent. We can expect considerable support.”
“Well, that’s true.”

“Since it became known that the family head would be inherited by the surviving third son, there are many who will find reasons to refuse support, so this marriage proposal is like a sacrificial offering to hell.”
“Not a blessing from heaven...? That sounds ominous…”
“Because it’s discarded land, haha.”
“That’s not something to laugh about!”
“However, if the duke’s support increases, you’ll have more time to dedicate to your studies, and this may be the only path for the Brave Family, which has been pushed to the brink of despair.”
Perhaps because I had been lamenting about my despair in bed, Sebas lined up such ominous words.
“The survivors are all working hard for the continuation of the Brave Family, so come on, Master, you must do your best too.”
Saying that, he smiled and pushed my back, but it truly felt like hell.
If I thought of it as for the sake of the family, it was somewhat better, and she was quite a beautiful woman, but her personality was terrible.

While it was understandable that she would insult the protagonist by saying, “You commoner scum,” she also used her entourage to bully harshly, and even after being married off to the frontier after her engagement was annulled, she didn’t give up.
Her hatred for the protagonist was the only emotion driving her to interfere repeatedly.
The duchess, consumed by hatred, ultimately makes a deal with a demon and transforms into a monstrous form to seek revenge, but if things continue like this, I would get caught up in that turmoil.
In my mind, I had knowledge of such a fate for Alicia.
No matter how much support I received from the duke’s family, what awaited me was nothing but certain doom.
Moreover, I didn’t appear at all in that game.
This meant that I would be killed by Alicia somewhere, which was way too dangerous.
“Alicia-sama will spend about a month here before returning to the academy with you, Master, so as a man of the Brave Family, please be sure to escort her properly.”
“Ah, uh…”
Sebas’s merciless words made me feel faint. My legs were giving way.
Living in the academy with a duchess whose personality had been twisted by turmoil felt like a new form of torture.

I had intended to attend the academy solely to build connections for the survival of the Brave Family, but being positioned as the fiancée of the woman who caused the turmoil felt like an impossible task.
“Waaahhhhhh!”
“That’s not good. You can’t go off to the dungeon or mountains to vent your frustrations now.”
I tried to bolt, but Sebas grabbed me by the neck and locked my joints.
“Ugh, rebellion! The crime is severe!”
“I can’t allow that. This falls under the category of discipline.”
Being firmly restrained and unable to move, Sebas truly was a capable butler serving the Brave Family.
The children of the Brave Family, due to their elite education, were unmanageable even for adults.
That’s why Sebas, who had taken care of such children, was strong.
“Master, I understand what you’re thinking, don’t I? I won’t allow you to take Alicia-sama to the dungeon. If an accident were to occur, the Brave Family would truly be finished.”
“Yes…”
But how could I avoid this doomed fate?
Dealing with enemy soldiers and monsters was far easier than dealing with a woman.
Ironically, I had been raised to be that way.
“It’s almost time, Master.”
“Damn it!”
Sebas stood me up, brushed off the dust from my clothes, and led me out.
As I was grumbling, the carriage carrying the duchess arrived in front of the mansion.
Since I held a lower title, I was expected to welcome her.
If I were to say something like “a small house like a commoner’s” or “why is someone of the duke’s status here in such a frontier,” I would receive a fist of iron as punishment.
When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
“Master, you must not show any murderous intent. This applies at the academy as well.”
“…Yes.”
I was hit on the head by Sebas and obediently suppressed my killing intent.
While there were no strict rules in our house, there was a mindset that if you regarded someone as an enemy, you could kill them without mercy.
So it was fine to show some killing intent.
There was also a saying that if you found a goblin, you should always search for and crush its settlement.
They breed like cockroaches and quickly form settlements, right?
If you don’t crush them before they grow big, it’ll lead to serious trouble.
“Look, they’re arriving. Stand up straight.”
“Yes!”
As the carriage came into view, I straightened my back.
The carriage carrying the duchess was smaller and more modest than I had expected.
“Is it small? I thought it would be a bigger carriage.”
“Indeed.”
I had expected that even if something went wrong, they would bring a lot of servants since it was a duke’s family.
I had cleaned the spare rooms for the servants, but it seemed it was all in vain.
Don’t underestimate a small mansion; the servants had all perished in battle and were now empty.
“Milady, this way, please.”
The carriage stopped in front of the mansion, and the man from the driver’s seat got down and opened the door to the passenger seat.
Out stepped a beautiful woman with translucent silver hair tied up in a bun—Duchess Alicia.
“Wow.”
The moment I saw her, I couldn’t help but let out such a voice.
Immediately, Sebas hit the back of my head.
“Master! …Ahem, welcome, Alicia-sama. I am Sebas, the butler. Please allow me to introduce myself.”
“…You’re reacting like that too, huh?”
Ignoring Sebas’s greeting, Alicia glared at me and muttered those words.
Upon closer inspection, there was a large burn scar from her left eye to her forehead.
“What happened to that burn?”
I asked out of concern, and Alicia lowered her face, looking pained.
But as expected of a duchess, even with a scar, she was quite beautiful.
There’s something about a beautiful woman who seems unfortunate that makes you want to protect her.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/FLcMwPd.jpeg
“Well, if you don’t want to talk about it, you don’t have to.”
I quickly corrected myself, realizing it would be pointless to ask something that might provoke her.
Sebas muttered beside me, “It’s too late now,” but since I managed to correct myself before she got angry, I considered it a safe move.
She had been sent here after causing a duel and an engagement annulment, so it was only natural that she bore scars from the battle. Moreover—
“In the Brave Territory, that’s quite normal.”
I smiled broadly to cover it up.
Yes, it was normal.

Soldiers heading to the battlefield or adventurers entering the mountains, both men and women, were covered in scars, and it was common for those who retired from such dangerous jobs to be missing fingers, arms, or legs in the Brave Territory.
A burn scar around the eyes was nothing to be surprised about… right?
It wasn’t something to be shocked over at this point.
By the way, I was also covered in scars if I took off my clothes, and I had a large scar on my forehead hidden by my bangs.
Sebas was also quite a formidable man if he took off his clothes.
“Well then, I’ll take my leave.”
“Ah, yes.”
As I was thinking about that, the driver placed a suitcase in front of the mansion gate and quickly returned.
It all happened so fast that I didn’t even have time to say anything.
Looking at Alicia, who was left behind, I thought, wait, is she really coming without a maid? She’s a young lady, after all.
Shouldn’t she at least have one familiar maid by her side? I realized her position was quite precarious.
To have our manpower diverted to take care of a duchess was honestly something that would interfere with various tasks, so I wanted them to send over a bit more help.
“Come, Alicia-sama, this way, please.”
Leaving me, who was dumbfounded watching the carriage leave, Sebas guided Alicia into the mansion with a forced smile.
Alicia didn’t even look back at the carriage that had brought her.
I had expected her to cast a resentful glance at the carriage, but contrary to my expectations, she remained quiet, as if she had accepted her fate.

Since the Brave Territory was despised by nobles as discarded land, I had thought the sheltered daughter would be in utter despair, and the fiancées of my deceased brothers had visited the mansion with faces filled with fear.
This was different from what I had imagined.
Her expression, which seemed to have given up on everything, resembled that of a captured soldier from the enemy country.
I couldn’t believe that someone with such an expression would go on to make a deal with a demon to interfere with the protagonists in the future, and I felt quite let down.
To be tempted by a demon, one needs to have darkness in their heart, and right now, she seemed devoid of any of the ominous, evil emotions I had seen in the game, burned out and pure white.
“Ah, just a moment, please.”
I called out to Alicia, who was heading into the mansion, and gently tapped her shoulder.
“…What? Was there dust on me? Sorry, it’s an old dress.”
“No, our place is much dustier, so it’s perfectly fine.”
“Eh…”
Alicia made a slightly displeased face at my words, but it felt more human.
Hmm, it was surprisingly easy to talk to her.
Since the Brave Family held a lower status, I had thought I would be subjected to various snide remarks as a villainous noble girl, but we were able to communicate.
Was this just because she had lost to a commoner and had her engagement annulled, leaving her pride in tatters?
Would there be a development where she would reignite her desire for revenge later on?
